title: nightwatch-roundup-nov-02-2028
body:
Nightwatch roundup (night ops): 2028-11-02
Owner: Aisha Patel (on-call lead)
Shift: 18:00 - 06:00 PT
Location: remote (EMEA overlap)

Quick summary:
- Quiet start, periodic latency spikes on /v1/generate-hosted between 22:40-23:10 PT tied to short cache thrash during an abnormal traffic spike from customer CUST-omega.
- One small degradation event at 00:14 PT: embedding-service1 GPU OOMs -> degraded capacity for 7m, automatic fallback to quantized variant worked but increased 95th latency.
- No customer-facing SEV; SLO blip recorded (p50 stable, p95 breached during window).

Incidents (timeline):
- 22:38 PT: An ops alert (latency-high) triggered for api-router-1; manual paging not required (automated mitigation engaged).
  - Root cause hypothesis: sudden short-lived surge of batched requests from a large customer job (CUST-omega); batch size distribution skewed, caused KV cache eviction and a transient queue build-up.
  - Mitigation: router autoscale added 2 pods, cache warmup run (kv-prefetch), request routing fallback to cheaper region (eu-west) for new requests.
  - Outcome: latency normalized 22:55 PT.
- 00:14 PT: embedding-service1 showed repeated GPU OOMs when a model upgrade job (internal training warmup) launched on shared pool.
  - Incident ID: SRE-2028-11-02-emb-1
  - Symptoms: GPU process crashes, instance restarted by k8s, rolling shift to quantized model variant on remaining capacity.
  - Duration: 00:14 - 00:21 PT (approx 7 minutes).
  - Customer impact: increased token latency for some embedding calls; no request failures (fallback worked).
  - Immediate actions taken: cordoned offending node, moved internal warmup to dedicated-dev pool, increased pod eviction thresholds to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

SLOs and metrics snapshot:
- infra SLO (API success 99.95% monthly): No sustained breach; short windows triggered alerting but monthly calc unaffected so far.
- latency SLO (p95 <= 300ms for hosted-gen baseline): p95 rose to 720ms during the 22:40-23:10 spike, and to ~1.1s during embedding fallback.
- Error budget: 1.2% remaining for the month after accounting for prior incidents; tracking in SLO dashboard (linked).
- Observations: KV cache miss rate increased ~4x during spike; batching effectiveness dropped (mean batch size halved) which increased per-token cost briefly.

Runbook / tooling notes (things we hit and will update):
- Router autoscaler threshold did its job but scaling cooldowns are slightly long causing micro-bursts to cascade. Action: proposal to reduce cooldown and add prewarm based on scheduled large-customer jobs (PR: infra#341).
- Embedding node affinity: need stronger isolation between internal training/warmup and production embedding serving pools. Created Jira: JIRA-SRE-8721 (isolation work).
- Add a short-circuit in the batching layer to refuse oversized batches from a single API key that would cause KV thrash. Possible follow-up: quick limiter change as interim.

On-call handoff notes (to day team):
- Passing to morning lead: Diego Ramirez at 06:00 PT.
- Open items for next shift:
  1) Finish cordon/drain verification for node gk-embed-09 (cordoned 00:25, still draining).
  2) Validate that CUST-omega job has been rate-limited; contact account team if not. Jira: CUST-OM-115.
  3) Merge quick autoscaler cooldown tweak (infra PR 341) to staging and run Canary.
  4) Follow up on noise-dev isolation ticket JIRA-SRE-8721 assigned to Lina.
- Slack threads to review: #ops-nightwatch, thread ts: 2028-11-02T00:20:00Z (link above in artifacts).

Action items and owners (short):
- Aisha: Draft post-incident timeline and add to incident board (due EOD 2028-11-03).
- Lina Ho: Start isolation plan in JIRA-SRE-8721, propose capacity reservations (due 2028-11-06).
- Owen Park: Run a simulated KV cache pressure test against staging and report results (due 2028-11-05).
- Diego: Validate autoscaler cooldown changes in staging and run smoke (due 2028-11-04).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider telemetry tag that marks "large-batch-caller" for accounts that repeatedly send big batches; helps routing decisions.
- Could we do cheap per-account micro-throttles in the request router to smooth bursts?
- Add checkpoint in deployment pipeline to detect model warmup jobs accidentally landing in prod pools. Might be a release-engineering policy gap.

Retro / what went well:
- Fallback to quantized variants worked as intended and prevented customer errors.
- Autoscaler prevented a full outage despite cooldown slowness.
- On-call collaboration was tight; handoff notes captured in real-time.

Retro / what to improve:
- Need faster telemetry for batch-size distribution on the router to detect big-job spikes earlier.
- Reduce scaling cooldown or add predictive prewarm for scheduled large jobs.
- Harder isolation between dev warmup traffic and prod serving.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Confluence Nightwatch runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Nightwatch+Runbook
- Incident board: https://jira.redwood.ai/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=58
- Infra PR for autoscaler: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/341
- Queue: JIRA-SRE-8721, CUST-OM-115

End of notes.

-- quick signoff: Aisha (on-call) 2028-11-03 08:12 PT
